newsitem.title: USA: C-Cor says will not meet Q2 expectations.
newsitem.headline: C-Cor says will not meet Q2 expectations.

text.p: C-Cor Electronics Inc said Tuesday its fiscal second quarter results will fall short of expectations due to delays in customer upgrades and shipping deferrals.
C-Cor said it is reducing its work force by 120 employees, or about 10 percent, and cutting other expenses.

Two factors contributing to the situation are continued delays in upgrades by several of C-COR's largest customers, and requests from customers to defer shipping dates as a result of changes in construction schedules or budgetary requirements, C-Cor said.
A company spokeswoman said the expectations for the second quarter, ending December 27, referred to by the company were those of analyst Jeff Sadler of Equitable Securities in Nashville,Tenn.
The spokeswoman, in a telephone interview, said Sadler had been expecting second quarter revenues of $35.5 million, and net income of $1.1 million, or $0.11 per share.
In the year-ago second quarter the company earned $0.07 per share.
In a press release, C-COR President and Chief Executive Officer Scott Chandler said the company plans operating expense reductions in all departments in order to improve gross margins.
C-Cor designs and manufactures electronic equipment used in a variety of communication networks worldwide.
